t_explain.answer:
Based on the provided document context, I'll explain the loan agreement in plain borrower-friendly language.

**What this agreement is about:**
You are borrowing $10,000 from the bank at an interest rate of 8% per year. The loan is to be repaid over a period of 3 years, with monthly payments of $313.36 starting from November 8, 2025.

**Your payments/obligations:**
You must make monthly payments of $313.36 on the 8th of every month until the loan is fully repaid. You can also make lump sum payments at any time without penalty. However, if you miss a payment or make a late payment, you may be charged a late fee of $25.

**Fees and penalties:**
There is a late fee of $25 if any payment is 10 days late. You may also be charged reasonable attorneys' fees if you default on the loan.

**What happens if you break the terms:**
If you fail to pay any part of the principal or interest as and when due, or if you become insolvent, the lender may declare the balance of the loan and the security (if any) immediately due and payable.

**Security:**
The loan amount is unsecured, which means you do not need to provide any collateral or security to the lender. However, if you breach the agreement, the lender may declare all sums due under the agreement immediately due and payable.

**Prepayment:**
You have the right to pay back the loan in full or make additional payments at any time without penalty.

**Governing law:**
This agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Massachusetts.

**Other important notes:**
The lender has the right to declare the balance of the loan and the security (if any) immediately due and payable if you default on the loan. You may also be charged reasonable attorneys' fees if you default on the loan.
